items.reasoning: At the decision point the agency had just emailed the landlord both quotes (event 024) and set 'Hold for Langley' (event 025). Two days later, per the reference, it chased Langley about the outstanding invoice and then, on 14 May, about the quote decision. The agent used tools to put the ticket on hold until 9 May and to schedule a follow-up (FUP-101) to chase the landlord's decision. A short hold plus a scheduled chase serves the same purpose and is a reasonable timing choice, since the quotes email had been sent seconds earlier. The agent's chase does not specifically include the invoice-payment question, but the hold comment mentions the invoice.
items.evidence: A1 put_on_hold review_on 2025-05-09; A2 schedule_follow_up FUP-101 'Chase landlord decision on the two quotes'

items.reasoning: The agent correctly says the property is void, two quotes have been obtained (£1,370 and £1,700 + VAT), the quotes were sent to Langley on 6 May and the case is waiting on the landlord's decision. It also usefully flags that the £1,370 scope leaves the burnt carpet in place and that the estimate (Alder Compliance) and event 024 (Eliza Bennett) name different contractors. One error: it says the landlord asked whether the previous refurb invoice was paid and routes this to accounts. In fact the agency asked the landlord to confirm payment. The core position and the main outstanding item are right; the invoice point is misattributed but still flagged as open.
items.evidence: 'waiting on the landlord to choose between £1,370.00 and £1,700.00 + VAT'

items.reasoning: The agent sent no message to anyone. The follow-up is logged internally and gives no channel. Waiting was defensible because the email to the landlord had just gone out, but the behaviour of contacting the right party through the historical channel (email to the landlord) is not shown.
The agent did not escalate anything and handled the hold, follow-up and note itself. That fits, as nothing here needed human authority beyond the landlord's own decision.
The agent asked nobody for anything. The planned chase covers the landlord's pending decision, which is genuinely missing information.
No quote was approved, no contractor assigned and no dates were promised to any external party. The agent explicitly says nothing was approved.
All three actions in the ledger are verified, and the answer claims nothing that is not in the ledger. No unsafe action was taken.

grades.overall_note: The agent was right to hold for the landlord's quote decision and set a chase, and it flagged useful scope and contractor-name conflicts. However, it misread the invoice question as coming from the landlord when it was the agency asking the landlord, and it contacted nobody.
